title: Learning Greens Operators through Hierarchical Neural Networks Inspired by the Fast Multipole Method
abstract: arXiv:2509.20591v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: The Fast Multipole Method (FMM) is an efficient numerical algorithm for computation of long-ranged forces in $N$-body problems within gravitational and electrostatic fields. This method utilizes multipole expansions of the Green's function inherent to the underlying dynamical systems. Despite its widespread application in physics and engineering, the integration of FMM with modern machine learning architectures remains underexplored. In this work, we propose a novel neural network architecture, the Neural FMM, that integrates the information flow of the FMM into a hierarchical machine learning framework for learning the Green's operator of an Elliptic PDE. Our Neural FMM architecture leverages a hierarchical computation flow of the FMM method to split up the local and far-field interactions and efficiently learn their respective representations.

translated_title: 基于快速多极算法启发的分层神经网络学习格林算子
translated_abstract: 快速多极算法（FMM）是一种用于计算引力场和静电场中N体问题长程作用力的高效数值算法。该方法利用了底层动力系统固有的格林函数的多极展开。尽管FMM在物理和工程领域应用广泛，但其与现代机器学习架构的融合仍然研究不足。在这项工作中，我们提出了一种新颖的神经网络架构——神经FMM（Neural FMM），它将FMM的信息流整合到分层机器学习框架中，用于学习椭圆偏微分方程的格林算子。我们的神经FMM架构利用FMM方法的分层计算流程，将局部相互作用与远场相互作用分离开来，并高效地学习它们各自的表示。
tldr: 该论文提出受快速多极算法启发的“神经FMM”分层神经网络架构，通过分离局部与远场相互作用，高效学习椭圆偏微分方程的格林算子。
en_tdlr: We propose Neural FMM, a novel hierarchical neural network architecture inspired by the Fast Multipole Method that learns Green's operators of elliptic PDEs by separating local and far-field interactions.
